answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes.
